# What Is Data? <br> Types &amp; Sources `r top_icon("database")`

---
### Focus of Day 8

.pull-left[.font100[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("layer-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Understanding** different types of data.
]
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Avoiding** biases in data collection.
]
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("pen-to-square", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Recording** data: best practices.
]
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("toolbox", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Reporting** data: tools to use.
]
]]

.pull-right[
<img src="assets/08-charts.png" style="width:100%; border-radius:6px;">
]

---
### What Is Data?

<div class="three-col">
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "2.4em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`</p>
    <p><strong>Evidence</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Information collected to examine hypotheses, address questions, or describe phenomena.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("cube", height = "2.4em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`</p>
    <p><strong>Foundation</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Transforms uncertainty into insight grounded in observable reality.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("clipboard-check", height = "2.4em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`</p>
    <p><strong>Replicable Conclusions</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Moves beyond opinion toward supported, replicable conclusions.</p>
  </div>
</div>

---
### Quantitative vs. Qualitative Data

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("hashtag", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Quantitative**

.font85[Information that can be **measured or counted** &mdash; expressed in numbers.]

- Test scores
- Survey ratings
- Hours spent on homework
- Growth measurements
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", fill = "#009E73")` Qualitative**

.font85[**Descriptive, non-numerical** information &mdash; provides context and depth.]

- Open-ended survey responses
- Observational notes
- Interview narratives
- Written explanations
]
]

---
### A Balanced Approach

<div class="three-col">
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("ruler-combined", height = "2.2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`</p>
    <p><strong>Quantitative Precision</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Measures patterns with numerical accuracy.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("comments", height = "2.2em", fill = "#009E73")`</p>
    <p><strong>Qualitative Depth</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Explains the <em>"why"</em> behind the patterns.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <p>`r fontawesome::fa("object-group", height = "2.2em", fill = "#c08a00")`</p>
    <p><strong>Integrated Research</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Combines approaches for a comprehensive understanding.</p>
  </div>
</div>

--

.content-box-yellow[
.font90[**The best projects mix both** &mdash; numbers show *what* is happening; words and context explain *why*.]
]

---
### Primary vs. Secondary Data

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("person-digging", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Primary Data**

.font85[Information you collect **directly**, through your own effort.]

- Experiments
- Surveys
- Interviews
- Observations
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("box-archive", fill = "#009E73")` Secondary Data**

.font85[Information that **already exists**, collected by others.]

- Books &amp; articles
- Websites
- Databases
- Government / agency records
]
]

---
### When to Use Each Type

<div class="three-col">
  <div class="col">
    <div class="content-box-blue">
    <p><strong>`r fontawesome::fa("1", fill="#4a7fb5")` Use Primary When…</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Your question is specific and unique &middot; you need fresh data nobody has &middot; you want control over how it's collected.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <div class="content-box-green">
    <p><strong>`r fontawesome::fa("2", fill="#009E73")` Use Secondary When…</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">The information already exists &middot; you need to save time &middot; you need broader context.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <div class="content-box-yellow">
    <p><strong>`r fontawesome::fa("3", fill="#c08a00")` Best Practice</strong></p>
    <p class="font80">Many strong projects use <strong>both</strong> types for a fuller understanding.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

---
### Data Structure &amp; Source

.pull-left[.font85[
**Structure &mdash; how it spans time:**

.content-box-blue[
- **Cross-sectional:** many units at **one** point in time (a snapshot).
- **Longitudinal:** the **same** units tracked **over time** (a movie).
]
]]

.pull-right[.font85[
**Source &mdash; where it comes from:**

.content-box-green[
- **Administrative:** records kept for operations (school enrollment, tax records).
- **Survey:** collected by asking people questions.
- **Experimental:** generated under controlled, randomized conditions.
]
]]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.font90[.center[.purple[*Knowing the structure and source tells you what claims the data can &mdash; and cannot &mdash; support.*]]]

---
### Data Quality Issues to Watch For

.font85[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Missing data** &mdash; *why* it's missing matters:

- **Missing at random** &mdash; gaps unrelated to the value itself; usually less harmful.
- **Missing not at random** &mdash; the missingness is *related* to the value (e.g., high earners skip the income question). This **biases** your results.
]

.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("ruler-horizontal", fill = "#c08a00")` Measurement error** &mdash; the recorded value differs from the true value (faulty instrument, vague question, typos).
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("clock-rotate-left", fill = "#009E73")` Historical limitations** &mdash; old data may use different definitions, categories, or methods than today &mdash; compare with care.
]
]

---
class: segue-yellow

# Data Quality &amp; <br> Common Mistakes `r top_icon("exclamation")`

---
### Common Mistakes in Research

.pull-left[.font90[
We can make mistakes at **every stage**:

- **Selecting participants** &rarr; *selection bias*
- **Collecting data** &rarr; *measurement &amp; response bias*
- **Analyzing data** &rarr; *confirmation bias*
- **Reporting results** &rarr; *reporting bias*
]]

.pull-right[
<img src="assets/08-survey.png" style="max-height:500px; border-radius:6px;">
]

---
### Biased Sampling &amp; Why Random Sampling Helps

.pull-left[.font85[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` Biased sampling**

*Example:* only surveying students who play sports about their favorite activities.

**Fix:** include students with diverse interests and backgrounds &mdash; use **random sampling** where possible.
]
]]

.pull-right[.font85[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("shuffle", fill = "#009E73")` Why random sampling helps**

- **Representative results** &mdash; findings reflect the whole population.
- **Reduced bias** &mdash; everyone has an equal chance of selection.
- **Statistical validity** &mdash; supports more accurate analysis.
]
]]

---
### Fixing Biased (Leading) Questions

.font90[A **leading question** pushes the respondent toward an answer. Rewrite it to be **neutral**.]

.font80[
| `r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` Biased question | `r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` Neutral alternative |
|---|---|
| "Don't you agree that school starts too early?" | "What time do you think school should start?" |
| "Why is the new lunch policy so unfair?" | "What are your thoughts on the new lunch policy?" |
| "How much do you hate doing homework?" | "How would you describe your experience with homework?" |
| "Wouldn't you prefer more recess time?" | "What is your opinion about the current recess time?" |
]

---
### Confirmation Bias

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("eye-low-vision", fill = "#c08a00")` The trap**

Only noticing the data that **supports** your hypothesis &mdash; and overlooking the rest.
]
]]

.pull-right[.font90[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", fill = "#009E73")` The fix**

Actively look for evidence that **contradicts** your expectations. Let the data change your mind.
]
]]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.font90[.center[.purple[*A good researcher tries to prove themselves **wrong** &mdash; not just right.*]]]

---
class: segue-green

# Accuracy in <br> Data Recording `r top_icon("pen")`

---
### Why Accurate Recording Matters

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-check", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Valid conclusions** &mdash; accurate data leads to trustworthy findings.
]
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("clone", fill = "#009E73")` Replicable research** &mdash; others can verify and build on your work.
]
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", fill = "#c08a00")` Research integrity** &mdash; honest recording reflects scientific ethics.
]
]]

.pull-right[
<img src="assets/08-recording.png" style="width:100%; border-radius:6px;">
]

---
### Data Recording Best Practices

<div class="card-grid">
  <div class="card">
    <h4>`r fontawesome::fa("bolt", fill = "#0148A4")` Record Immediately</h4>
    <p>Don't rely on memory &mdash; write down observations right away.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>`r fontawesome::fa("table-list", fill = "#0148A4")` Use Standardized Forms</h4>
    <p>Create consistent templates for data collection.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>`r fontawesome::fa("camera", fill = "#0148A4")` Document Visually</h4>
    <p>Take photos or videos when appropriate.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>`r fontawesome::fa("cloud-arrow-up", fill = "#0148A4")` Back Up Your Data</h4>
    <p>Keep multiple copies in different locations.</p>
  </div>
</div>

---

### Evening Work Period `r fontawesome::fa("book", fill="#0148A4", height="0.8em")` 7:00 &ndash; 9:00 PM

.pull-left[.font82[
**Individual + partner work** during CTD RTA study hours. TA available for drop-in questions.

- **Individual DataCORE Journal:** describe the **shape** of your data distribution. Is it skewed? Are there outliers? What might explain them?

- **(RcS):** create a **correlation matrix** for your key variables. Screenshot and annotate &mdash; which correlations are strongest? Do they make sense theoretically?

- **Slide update:** revise your **Methods slide** with what you now know about your data &mdash; be specific about dataset name, timeframe, and sample.
